newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch plan sharp rise of renewable energy by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Dutch plan sharp rise of renewable energy by 2000.

text.p: The Dutch government on Tuesday set out a programme designed rapidly to boost the use of renewable energy within three years, the ministry of economic affairs said on Tuesday.

The programme, presented to the lower house by Economic Affairs Minister Hans Wijers, aims to ensure that three percent of Dutch energy should come from renewable sources by the year 2000. At the moment only one percent comes from renewables.
The measures spelt out in the paper "Renewable energy on the march" include:
- making 95 million guilders available per year for research and development from 1997 to reduce the price of renewable energy, .
- a "green" tax and other financial incentives to stimulate market penetration.
- from 2001, government may set a compulsory minimum level of energy that distribution companies supply from renewables.
- more urgent tackling of practical problems, such as the location of wind-driven power stations.
